title: Fromagerie Martin’s Starter Drift Dilemma

scenario.title: Fromagerie Martin’s Starter Drift Dilemma
scenario.setting: Nestled in the sun-dappled Loire Valley farmlands, the three-generational Fromagerie Martin has produced award-winning goat crottin for 72 years using a single carefully guarded starter culture passed down through the family. New apprentice Jules has taken to storing a weekly starter batch in a stainless steel bin instead of the family’s traditional cedar crock, altering the culture’s ambient exposure. Farm owner Elara and long-time cheesemaker Papa Tom have clashed over whether to correct Jules or risk losing the dairy’s signature tang.

characters.name: Elara Martin
characters.tendencies: She runs the shop’s front counter, fields customer orders, and prioritizes preserving the farm’s iconic signature flavor over hasty changes to the family’s legacy.

characters.name: Papa Tom Lefevre
characters.tendencies: He’s the retired 70-year-old head cheesemaker who speaks with the unfiltered voice of the farm’s 72-year history and demands strict adherence to the original starter process.

characters.name: Jules Moreau
characters.tendencies: He’s the eager new apprentice who studied modern cheese-making techniques and modified the starter storage to suit his culinary training.

turns.name: Elara Martin
turns.text:
Bonjour, mademoiselle! I saved you a fresh portion of our award-winning signature goat cheese, aged exactly two weeks in our cellar per Great-Grandmother’s recipe. We didn’t cut any corners this season to keep that iconic, earthy Loire Valley flavor you raved about last month.
[Wraps the sliced cheese in crinkly brown parchment paper tied with a strip of twine harvested from the farm’s hemp rows]

turns.name: Papa Tom Lefevre
turns.text:
Now hold up, youngster—that’s not how you ladle the curds gently. We’ve clung to this exact same starter process since Grandpapa Martin first set up our vat back in 1951, and rushing this step will ruin the earthy, floral finish that won us our first regional award.
[He raps his weathered knuckles against a stack of hand-carved wooden cheese molds, then reaches for a crock of pale, tangy mother starter to add a splash to the fresh curd batch.]

turns.name: Jules Moreau
turns.text:
Chef Martin, I wanted to show you the tweaks I made to the starter storage last night! I installed insulated metal racks with calibrated heat mats to keep the goat and cow cultures at a steady, ideal temp instead of them swinging with the Loire Valley’s weather. I also labeled every jar with the culture strain and harvest date so we can nail down exact ripening timelines moving forward.
[Pausing to tap the digital temperature readout mounted above the rack, grinning widely as the screen flickers to show a steady 43°F]

turns.name: Elara Martin
turns.text:
"Papa, easy now—don’t harp on my curd ladling just yet. Let Jules share what he’s put together first; I know we’ve stuck to Great-Grandmot’s exact recipe for decades, but I don’t want to write off an idea before we see if it keeps our signature flavor intact."
[Leans against the weathered pine prep counter, tucking a stray sun-bleached strand of hair behind her ear while setting down her curd ladle for a moment.]

turns.name: Papa Tom Lefevre
turns.text:
Cut that out right now, Jules. Those insulated racks and heat mats are nothing but modern foolery that’ll ruin the starter’s delicate, decades-old colony. We’ve stuck to this exact same process for three generations, and we ain’t throwing it off now.
[He swats Jules’ experimenting hand away from the starter storage bin, then grabs his well-worn wooden starter spoon from the bench to jab at the original wicker shelves lining the cool cellar walls.]

turns.name: Jules Moreau
turns.text:
I installed insulated metal racks with calibrated heat mats to keep our mother starter at the exact steady temperature Great-Grandmot documented, no more random afternoon draft fluctuations throwing off its consistency. I didn’t tamper with the traditional curd ladling process Papa Tom swears by at all, just fixed this tiny storage flaw I noticed last week.
[He gestured over his shoulder toward the open cellar doorway, holding up a small digital temperature readout to display the locked-in 18°C setting he’d calibrated overnight.]

dm_opening: DM opening: the cast gathers around a question the scene has been carrying for a year.
dm_closing: DM closing: the Elara Martin holds the line; the next session's hook waits at the door.
